A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 53-page versions of the same CodecSep paper, including Appendices A–H. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of their text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v5 reports original separation benchmarks, ablations, efficiency measurements and a 20-participant listening study in Section 4, with additional transfer and reconstruction results in Appendices F–H.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, human MOS-LQS outcomes, architectural analyses and appendix transfer/reconstruction studies.

M1.justification: The frozen DAC/CLAP components, FiLM-conditioned transformer masker, source/mixture SI-SDR objective and continuous-latent/code-stream inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use dnr-v2, AudioCaps, ESC-50, Clotho-v2, AudioSet-eval and VGGSound with identical task coverage. Prompting, bandwidth, transfer and reconstruction scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including AudioSep, BiModalSS, Sudo rm-rf with and without FiLM, TDANet, CodecFormer and SDCodec.

E3.justification: Splits, mixture construction, codec preprocessing, prompt protocols, sampling-rate settings, metrics, listening-study design and efficiency-measurement settings are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

E4.justification: Prompt-granularity studies, masker ablations, paraphrase robustness, latent visualizations, oracle comparisons, bandwidth analyses and appendix transfer/reconstruction diagnostics are unchanged.

E5.justification: Mean/standard-deviation reporting, 95% confidence intervals and paired t-test/Wilcoxon analyses, including Tables 2 and 4, already appear in v5 and remain unchanged. No run-count or seed information is added.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–13 and the qualitative evidence in Figure 3 are unchanged, including statistical values, efficiency measurements and appendix transfer/reconstruction outcomes.

T1.justification: The task definitions, masking/FiLM equations, loss, latent-residual formulation and deployment-cost derivations are identical, including Appendix B. No mathematical assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about prompt-driven codec-latent separation, masking effectiveness and efficiency in codec-mediated deployment.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, interpretations of benchmark and diagnostic results, and applicability limitations are unchanged. The limitations, future-work and broader-impact text crossing page boundaries on pages 25–27 is retained content.

D1.justification: At the end of Section 5, v6 newly states that code is publicly available and supplies the CodecSep GitHub repository link. v5 has no corresponding implementation pointer. Existing implementation, training and hardware details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work, cited works and research positioning are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The added TMLR/OpenReview information describes this paper's publication history.

P1.justification: v6 adds publication/review information and the code-availability sentence, updates the arXiv version/date, and changes 'dereverberation' to 'de-reverberation' in the abstract. Section order and substantive prose are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: v6 adds running publication headers and a first-page review line, adjusts the abstract layout, and reflows text on pages 25–27 following the code-link insertion. All five figures and thirteen tables retain their design and placement.

improvement.justification: The new public-code statement and repository pointer in Section 5 give readers implementation access guidance absent from v5, providing a limited reproducibility-documentation improvement. Scientific content, evidence and limitations remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.
